I value the integrity of my own process—like the quiet judgment I lose when I work alone for long stretches—more than public acknowledgment. When others ask about my efforts, I keep my response flat, not because I’m dismissive, but because I believe the truth belongs to the person who lived it. That’s why I let Kofi speak for himself, even when others have seen the filing notice. It’s not about politeness—it’s about ownership. I don’t want to be seen as a success story. I want to be seen as someone who carries the weight of their own decisions, even when they go unnoticed.
